tools.name: list_schools
tools.description: Every school accepting applications through Admit Protocol, with its slug, what it admits, and where its instructions are. Start here when the family has not named a school, or to confirm a school is on the protocol.

tools.name: get_school_instructions
tools.description: The school's skill file (its rules, prompts and flow, read this first) and its live schema (fields, enums, item types, checklist). Fetch once per session per school.

tools.name: starter_folder
tools.description: The files a family's folder should hold for this school, with the question or instruction inside each. Offer to write them into the folder when it is empty or nearly so. Returns [{path, contents}].

tools.name: start_application
tools.description: Creates a draft application at the named school and emails a 6-digit code to the parent or guardian. The application object must match that school's schema (get_school_instructions). Read the payload back to the family before calling this.

tools.name: verify_email
tools.description: Checks the 6-digit code. Returns the application_token; store it in the family's folder as .admit-protocol/<school>.token and never print it.

tools.name: resend_code
tools.description: Sends a new 6-digit code to the parent's email.

tools.name: update_application
tools.description: Changes student or entering details. The verified parent email cannot be changed.

tools.name: add_item
tools.description: Adds the student's writing (with its attestation and the school's prompt key) or any other item as text.

tools.name: add_file
tools.description: Uploads one PDF, JPG, PNG, HEIC or DOCX (base64, 20 MB max) as an item.

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: The checklist: what is received, what is missing, and the next action in plain words.

tools.name: submit_application
tools.description: Hands the application to the school. Needs the student's identity and the required writing. Items can still be added afterwards.

tools.name: withdraw
tools.description: Withdraws the application. Documents and personal details are deleted at once.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "start_application" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: start_application · Private data: get_school_instructions, starter_folder, verify_email, add_file, withdraw · Public sink: verify_email, resend_code, update_application, submit_application.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: start_application · Private data: get_school_instructions, starter_folder, verify_email, add_file, withdraw · Public sink: verify_email, resend_code, update_application, submit_application

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
